newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH CALL MONEY RATES STICK TO HIGH LEVELS.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH CALL MONEY RATES STICK TO HIGH LEVELS.

text.p: Dutch call money rates were stuck at recent high levels on Friday, which surprised market players since the Central bank's new allocation to the money market was seen as sufficient.
The Dutch central bank allocated 3.47 billion guilders to the money market this morning under a seven-day special advances pact at an unchanged rate of 2.90 percent.
Individual banks' applications up to 3.50 billion guilders were met for 13.5 percent. Above that level no subscriptions were awarded.
Call money was bid at 3.06 to 3.18 percent.
Dealers said the rate for overnight money was likely to fall after the weekend.
"But as the current credit quota is expiring next week we can not be sure whether call money will come down," said one dealer.
Towards the expiry of a credit quota, commercial banks tend to build up savings under the scheme, which can put pressure on call money just before the quota expires.
"There should be enough liquidity in the market, but it all depends on the distribution if liquidity," said one dealer.
Other rates were unchaged, while the guilder was a touch stronger versus the German mark.
The guilder was trading at 112.44 per 100 marks from 112.455 on Thursday.
